usefulness.rationale: The dossier gives a coherent picture of who Ana Botín is: born 1960 in Santander, Bryn Mawr economics graduate, J.P. Morgan start, Santander from 1988, Banesto and Santander UK leadership, Executive Chair of Banco Santander since September 2014, plus her foundation work (Fundación CYD, Empieza por Educar), board roles, the €7.5bn share sale, and current thinking on AI and education backed by 2025–2026 press coverage. A reader clearly learns who she is and what she has done. However, the dossier never states what it does not know: there is no explicit gap or uncertainty note, and several undated or dated claims (Coca-Cola board, MIT advisory board, 2015-era profile details, a 2021 Fortune ranking) are presented without flagging whether they still hold. It is reasonably meeting-ready — current role, recent public statements and priorities are all present — but a reader would have to guess which biographical details are current versus historical, and the dossier includes low-quality material (a conspiracy-themed archive.org source, placeholder 'statement' claims) without explaining its reliability.
